sections.title: Agents (overview)
items: “Start new agent”: pick a folder; the agent starts and gets going at once with its start request (e.g. the AI-Connect watcher). Resuming starts without it.
Sorting cards: drag at a free spot with the mouse; with a finger, hold briefly first. The order is the same on every device.
Context ring: green below 50 %, amber above, red from 70 % – time for /compact or a new conversation soon.
Effort slider and ultracode apply per project folder. A running Claude takes the new level without a restart once its current answer is done; background tasks keep running.
Quota at the top: Claude's used five-hour and weekly limits, once a session has reported them.

“Start” on the card: the permission mode the agent starts in – Ask, Edit (file edits without asking), Auto or Plan. Auto by default; applies from the next start, inside the agent Shift+Tab switches it.
When an agent asks for permission, its card shows the command with “Allow” and “Deny”. The terminal asks the same; the first answer counts.
“Changes” (branch icon, on the card and in the header of every terminal) shows what the agent changed in the project: changed, new and deleted files since the last commit; a tap shows the diff.

From the configured context size on (50 % by default) the card advises a handover to a fresh session, a notification says so once; “Ask for a handover” asks the agent for a handover document. The settings menu can make this automatic.

“Start in a worktree of its own” (start dialog): the agent works in a second working copy on a new branch next to the project; once it has ended, “Remove worktree” on the card removes it again – without losing unsaved work.
⟳ (card and terminal bar) restarts the agent and resumes its conversation, e.g. when it hangs or should read changed settings. It asks first; a running answer and background tasks end.

Clock on the card: schedule a prompt for later, e.g. “run the tests and report” at 7 am. It is typed in at that time once the agent is idle; scheduled prompts are listed on the card and removed with ×.
When a Claude agent runs into its usage limit, Agent-Orc schedules the resume for the next reset of the quota (yellow entry on the card). Is it still limited then, the next reset follows.
“To several” (next to the workspaces, from two running agents on): send the same prompt to several agents, e.g. “commit and push”.

“>_” (card and terminal bar) opens a plain terminal in the project folder, also next to the running agent; if one runs already, it opens that one. Please do not start a second agent in the same folder there.

sections.title: Workspaces
items: All workspaces live on the server: every device shows the same, and changes appear everywhere at once. “Default” is the one workspace without a name. An agent stands in exactly one workspace; add it to another and it leaves the old one.
Type a name at the top and press Enter: the unnamed workspace becomes a named one (the unnamed one is empty again afterwards) and shows up in the overview and in the bar of every workspace.
Clicking another workspace jumps to the tab that already shows it (↗︎), otherwise this tab switches. A middle click opens a new tab.
Jumping only finds tabs opened from within Agent-Orc – so open further workspaces through the buttons; they can then be detached onto other monitors.
On the phone (installed app) the bar switches within the same window.
“+” adds a running agent as a column, “− n +” sets how many columns fill the screen.
Dragging a column head sorts the columns; dragging the divider on its right edge changes the width, a double click resets it.
Shortcuts on a computer: Alt+Shift+1 … 9 jumps to that column, Alt+Shift+← / → to the previous or next workspace.
On a phone the workspace shows one column at a time; a sideways swipe in the terminal brings the next (to the left) or previous one (to the right), up and down scrolls.
Tile icon at the top left: all pages (agents, files, consumption …) – the workspace has no bar at the bottom, so the terminal gets the room.
Fullscreen (four-corner icon): terminal and input field only, where possible without the browser bars too; the small button at the top right brings everything back.
On a phone the header is one row; the other workspaces sit behind the arrow next to the name, and the terminal bar names the column and closes it with ×.

sections.title: Terminal
items: Input field at the bottom: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
Microphone: dictation through Whisper; the GPU is done at once, the CPU is slower but always there. If it fails, “Retry” sends the same recording again.

Paperclip: take a photo, pick a picture or screenshot from the gallery, capture the screen (desktop) or attach a file – it lands in the project folder and it shows as a small preview above the input field (× removes it) and goes to the agent with the next message. A screenshot from the clipboard can also simply be pasted into the input field (Ctrl+V).
Grip on the right (jog): pull up or down to scroll, the further the faster. Mouse wheel and swiping scroll as well.

Font size: one for all terminals of this device – in the ☰ menu (also in the workspace header) or, on phones, in the ⋮ menu of the terminal bar. On phones ⋮ also holds restart, terminal, project folder, changes and the text view for selecting and copying.
The key bar sends Esc, Tab, arrows, Ctrl and so on – Ctrl and Alt apply to the next key.
Templates (in the paperclip menu): put frequent prompts into the input field with a tap; “Manage templates” creates them, for all devices.
File paths in the output (e.g. src/main.py:42) are clickable when they exist: files open in the editor at that line, folders in the file view. The folder icon at the top opens the project folder.
Editor: Markdown shows as a page (pencil: edit), pictures as pictures; other files that are not text can be downloaded. “Back” returns to where the file was opened from.
Extra keys: the arrow at the end of the first row folds or unfolds the other rows (for every terminal of the device).

Arrange extra keys (☰ menu): drag keys into order, also between rows, add ready-made keys, record a key combination (e.g. Ctrl+R) or create a text key that types a fixed text such as /compact and sends it if wanted. The arrangement holds for every device; “reset” brings back the config’s keys.

sections.title: Consumption
items: Tokens from all Claude conversations on this machine, per day, project and model, for 7, 14 or 30 days – from the terminal, VS Code and subagents too.

sections.title: Settings (☰)
items: Font, font size, line spacing and lines per scroll step – stored on this device.

Push messages: switch them on per device in the ☰ menu. You then get a message when an agent is done or waits for a permission or an answer; tapping it opens the agent. Only over HTTPS; on iPhones only in the installed app.
Dictation engine: default or one of the engines the Whisper service offers (e.g. Parakeet: fast; Whisper) – per device.

permission.label: Start
permission.title: Permission mode the agent starts in: Ask (before edits and commands), Edit (file edits without asking), Auto (Claude decides what is safe), Plan (plans only). Applies from the next start; inside the agent Shift+Tab switches it.

push.unsupported: Only over HTTPS; on iPhones only in the installed app.
push.denied: Notifications are blocked in the browser – allow them in its site settings.
